meaning:
ὑπο-τάσσω
[in LXX for דָבַר hi., דָּמַם, שׂוּם, שִׁית, etc. ;]
1. as a military term, to place or rank under (Polyb.).
2. to subject, put in subjection: 1Co.15:27, Php.3:21, Heb.2:5, 8; pass., Rom.8:20, 1Co.15:27-28, 1Pe.3:22, Eph.1:22. Mid., to subject oneself, obey: absol., Rom.13:5, 1Co.14:34; with dative of person(s), Luk.2:51 10:17, 20, Rom.8:7 10:3 13:1, 1Co.14:32 15:28 (ὑποταγήσεται; cf. M, Pr., 163), 1Co.16:16, Eph.5:21-22 (T, WH, txt., R, om.), Eph.5:24, Col.3:18, Tit.2:5, 9 3:1, Heb.12:9, 1Pe.2:18 3:1 3:5 5:5; imperat., Jas.4:7, 1Pe.2:13 5:5.†
(AS)

renderings.kjv: hey are commanded to be under obedience

elsewhere.note: And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth. He was subject to them, and his mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
because the mind of the flesh is hostile toward God; for it is not subject to God’s law, neither indeed can it be.
The spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets,
He put all things in subjection under his feet, and gave him to be head over all things for the assembly,
who will change the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working by which he is able even to subject all things…
Wives, be in subjection to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
to be sober minded, chaste, workers at home, kind, being in subjection to their own husbands, that God’s word may not be blasphemed.
For he didn’t subject the world to come, of which we speak, to angels.
